note_tweet.text:
You don't know how to use AI agents if you're not using @orca_build.

I used to laugh at OpenAI Dots and Grok Bot. Why would anyone want a bot when you already have terminals?

Now I barely touch a terminal. Everything runs from my phone through 1 Orca bot (379 chats so far):

I don't care what harness is running what anymore. Antigravity, Codex, Claude Code, Factory Droid, and OpenCode all work in 1 place, and everything just fucking works.

I drop a rough idea from my phone. My main bot takes it from there, spins up isolated git worktrees for each repo so nothing collides, and routes every piece to the right harness and model. Gemini 4 Neon or Claude Opus 5.5 handle heavy code, GPT-6.2-Astra does deep research, and DeepSeek v4.1 Flash runs cheap scout swarms and supervises other workers.

Subagents spawn their own subagents. Workers message each other directly when a task finishes or needs input, check GitHub PRs, move Linear tickets, and open their own built-in browser to verify pages. My bot only pings me with a decision button when I actually need to step in.

Right now I'm running bare-metal experiments, 3D demos, custom kernels, and research swarms in parallel from my phone while agents coordinate each other in the background.

If you're still switching between 5 CLI tabs and copy-pasting context by hand, try an Orca bot for 2 days. You won't go back to babysitting terminals.

note_tweet.text:
Grok Bot 团队工程师 Lauren Tan（网友叫她「土豆姐」）上周四发了一篇长文，讲怎么把活真正交给
Bot。不到一周，309 万次浏览、3.3 万人收藏，马斯克亲自转发，配文是「把 Grok Bot 当成一个特别
聪明的员工来用」。

她想纠正的迷思是：很多人派活时一开口就是「帮我填这张表」「帮我回这封邮件」——这是把流程当成
了目标。

01 先想清楚目标
填表、发邮件只是流程里的一步。往上多想一层：这件事最终是为了多赚钱，还是少花钱？目标说清了，
Bot 才会奔着结果去，有时还能找到比原来更省事的路子。
提示词：
「嗨，土豆，以后这件事就交给你了。根据这个目标，给自己起个名字，再挑一张头像吧。」
目标说不清时，反过来让它问你：
「我有件事想交给你，但还没想好目标该怎么描述。你多问我几个问题，直到我们一起定下一个我满意的
目标。」
这一招不只对 Bot 有用——写方案、定选题、梳需求，想不清就先让 AI 反问你。

02 把流程一口气说给 Bot 听
最推荐的办法是打开语音输入，想到哪儿说到哪儿，不用提前整理。最好说清六件事：平时怎么做、
哪里要留意、用到哪些应用工具、怎么检查活干得对不对、信息从哪来（邮件/工单/网站）、反馈从
哪来（客户评价/同事意见）。
说完先别开工，让它复述：
「先别急着干活，用大白话复述一遍你理解的目标和流程，我看看有没有需要补充或者纠正的地方。」
来回聊几轮捋顺了再执行。

03 教会 Bot 你平时怎么判断
很多判断你都是下意识做的，Bot 当然不知道。比如安排预约，你知道哪些服务耗时、什么时候该多留
缓冲；邮件和预约系统时间对不上该信哪个；邮件发出去了也不代表预约完成——信息录入正确、客户
收到确认，才算完事。
做法是先给几个真实例子，尤其是以前出过错的，再问它会怎么处理，然后告诉它对不对。
提示词（关键那句别删）：
「帮我看看，这个流程里还有哪些地方是我没交代清楚的。重点问问我平时怎么做判断、从哪儿拿信息、
怎么确认活干得对不对，以及什么情况需要找我。一次只问一个问题。」
要是一次甩十个问题，你的注意力就不够用了。

04 让 Bot 自己越干越好
不用每次亲自纠错，让 AI 自己收反馈。比如负责预约的 Bot，就让它盯邮箱和点评网站：有顾客说
等太久，它调出当天记录，多半能定位卡在哪。数据越全，建议越准。连收集数据的工具都能让 Bot
自己开发——比如汽修店，让它搭个应用记录到店、接待、接钥匙、修完的时间点。

05 设好 routine，到点自己开工
routine 就是定时任务。不设的话只有你叫它才动；设好之后到点或遇事件就自己开工，一条 Slack
消息、一封发到 Bot 专属邮箱的邮件都能叫醒它。
注意额度：每小时跑一次、或者拿热闹的 Slack 频道当触发条件，一天就能烧完一周额度。间隔拉长、
条件收窄，额度更耐用；周额度快用完时，先暂停不用的 routine，再让 Bot 放宽间隔、收窄触发，
别急着升级套餐。

懒得自己搭？导入 Dr Eggbot
土豆姐把自己的经验教给了一个叫 Dr Eggbot 的智能体，在 Bot 市场点 Import Bot 就能导入，它会先
问几个偏好问题再帮你搭。它遵循几条原则：一个 Bot 只干一件事、口吻固定、写清哪些事不干（负责
起草的只写不发，没什么可说就不出声）。v2 版还自带两个体检任务：工作日扫对话里的卡壳点，每周
一查 token 有没有浪费。

最后是 Bob 大叔的评论：「一开始你压根不知道拿 Bot 干什么，后来想到一个挺傻的点子，成了，又想
到第二个。不知不觉你手上已经有一整套 Bot 环环相扣，然后你还得再用一个 Bot 去给它们之间的连接
调优、重构。」

几点补充：Grok Bot 从 X Premium（30 美元/月起）就包含；没开通也能把同一套思路套到 Meta Muse、
ChatGPT Dots 这类个人智能体上。方法本身不绑定平台，绑定的是「先定目标、再拆流程、再教判断」
这个顺序。

#GrokBot #AI智能体 #提示词 #马斯克 #自动化 #AI员工

Official @obsdmd, Nov 26 05:19 Asia/Shanghai: Obsidian now has official connectors for every agent, so agents can share a knowledge base while you keep ownership of the data.

I’m dating this carefully. Official Obsidian Help is at https://t.co/jzhZqv2LI0. Official roadmap lists Skills as launched in November 2026, with no calendar day. Official GitHub releases for obsidianmd/obsidian-skills show the package rolling out earlier this month — 1.1.0 on Nov 11, then directory updates through 1.2.2 and 1.2.3 on Nov 25 UTC. I’m treating this morning’s official post as the public connectors announcement, not as the first day the repo existed.

Official, from that post, the official Help page, and official follow-up replies:

1. Official post: you can switch agents, let them collaborate, and organize knowledge as notes, diagrams, canvas, tables, kanban, and more. Official: what you create is saved locally on your devices, in open-format files you own and can use offline. Official: Obsidian has no built-in AI, no account required, and cannot access your data. Official: you can use it completely AI-free — that is the default.
2. Official Help: connectors can teach an agent to write Obsidian Flavored Markdown (wikilinks, embeds, callouts, properties), create and edit Bases and Canvas files, search and manage notes in the running app with Obsidian CLI, and sync or publish vaults without the desktop app using Obsidian Headless. Official Help names Claude, ChatGPT, Antigravity, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Grok Bot, Hermes, Kiro, Muse, OpenCode, and others. Official install directories include Claude, ChatGPT, Dots, Cursor, Grok Bot, Hermes, and Kiro. Official: the ChatGPT plugin also works in Codex and Dots.
3. Official Help privacy: “Obsidian connectors don't send anything by themselves. When an agent uses them, the notes it reads become part of the conversation and are processed by the AI model you use.” Official: review your agent’s privacy policy before you point it at a vault with sensitive notes. Official Help: the Markdown, Bases, and Canvas skills only describe file formats, so they work in any agent that can read and write files in your vault; the CLI skill needs the desktop app running with Obsidian CLI turned on.
4. Official replies from @obsdmd: OpenClaw is officially supported. Mistral is supported if you point it at the official repo. Official: MCP for agents that only support MCP is on the roadmap — I’m not calling that shipped.

I have not connected an agent to a vault yet. If I try this, I will add the official Claude or ChatGPT plugin, point it at one small test vault with nothing sensitive in it, and log whether the agent can create a note I can actually open in Obsidian.

https://t.co/RqJaMgOakR
https://t.co/KG94m1tUYw

note_tweet.text:
🤖 马斯克转发的 Grok Bot 攻略，藏着一套培养 AI 员工的方法。

核心观点只有一句话：

别把 Bot 当工具使唤，要把它当成一个聪明的员工来培养。

有人只拿它查资料、写周报，有人养了一群 AI 员工替自己打工：一位网页设计师让几个 Bot 分别运维服务器、设计网页、照着他的文风写稿，几周就干完了几年的活。

✅ 它能帮你干什么？
✓ 把重复流程整个接过去，从目标到执行，不用你一步步盯
✓ 替你盯邮箱、点评和工单，自己找问题、自己改流程
✓ 到点自己开工：定时、Slack 消息、邮件都能把它叫醒

📌 别给 Bot 派任务，给它一个目标。

📌 五步养一个 AI 员工，操作步骤如下
1️⃣ 先定目标，别给流程：新建一个 Bot，没想好名字就先叫它「土豆」，以后再让它自己改名。发这句：嗨，土豆，以后<你的目标>这件事就交给你了。根据这个目标，给自己起个名字，再挑一张头像吧。目标一时说不清，就让它反过来问你，问到你们一起定下来为止。
2️⃣ 把流程语音倒给它：打开语音输入，一口气说清平时怎么做、注意什么、用了哪些工具、怎么检查对不对、信息从哪来、反馈从哪来。说完先别让它干，让它用大白话复述一遍目标和流程，确认没理解错再开工。
3️⃣ 教它你下意识的判断：给几个真实例子，尤其以前出过错的；让它一次只问一个问题，找出你没交代清楚的地方。记住：邮件发出去了不算完，录入正确、客户收到确认才算完。
4️⃣ 让它自己越干越好：接上邮箱和点评网站，让它自己读反馈、自己找问题、自己提改进。连收集数据的工具，都可以让它帮你搭。
5️⃣ 设 routine 到点开工：在对话里用大白话告诉它什么时候干、什么触发。别设太勤：每小时跑一次，一天可能就烧完一周的额度。

🛠️ 懒得从零搭建？

可以直接从 Grok Bot 市场导入 Lauren Tan 制作的 Dr Eggbot。

它相当于一个 Bot 设计师，会先询问你的需求，再帮你创建合适的 Bot。

⚠️ 重要提醒：

Grok Bot 包含在 X Premium 订阅里，每月 30 美元起；没开通也没关系，同样思路套到 Meta Muse、ChatGPT Dots 这类个人智能体上，一样好用。负责起草的 Bot 只写不发，哪些事不干要在 Bot 里写清楚。

📌 真正厉害的不是拥有多少个 Bot，而是有多少重复工作不再需要你亲自做。

如果给你配一个 AI 员工，你最想把哪件工作交给它？

If you're into AI and want to stay ahead of where agents are heading, this is a must-read. https://t.co/WrJhHiJQI7

note_tweet.text:
Grok Bot is a general always-on agent on its own cloud computer. It browses, clicks, and runs any workflow (no APIs needed), learns from screen recordings, and keeps working while your devices are off. Multiple bots run in parallel. Starts at $30/mo.

Claude Code is a specialized coding agent. It reads your full repo, plans multi-file changes, edits, tests, and iterates inside your terminal or IDE. Best for deep software work, not broad automation. Included on Claude Pro (~$20/mo).

OpenAI Dots (likely “GOT Dots”) are also always-on agents with their own cloud computer and 4000+ app connectors. Similar persistent style to Grok Bot, but entry starts at $100/mo on ChatGPT Pro and ties tightly into the OpenAI ecosystem.

Grok Bot prioritizes flexible, low-friction personal automation across any tool. Claude Code owns coding depth. Dots sit in the same always-on category but at a higher price point.

note_tweet.text:
This time of year, we start thinking about how we can give back.

My partners @alex_karnal , @nick_myerberg  and I talk a lot about what we can achieve when the right technology is pointed at seemingly intractable problems.

One dynamic we have spent a lot of time on is the conundrum of medicine adherence. There are amazing medicines available that can help us prevent disease, yet the data reveals that we all consistently have trouble maintaining the habit of taking our daily or weekly medicine.

Along the way, we stumbled on another similar human dynamic that seemed like it might have a solution rooted in emerging technology.

Most people want to help others, and nearly everyone feels better after they do. But daily life tends to get in the way. Enter the possibilities of emerging personal AI agents like @Meta  Muse, @OpenAI  Dots, OpenClaw, Grok Bot, and others. Over the last several weeks, we started to ask:

What if personal AI could help people not just do more, but do more good?

So, in advance of this Thanksgiving holiday, a group of us built and are now releasing a first answer:

https://t.co/SdVXD4fOXr

Simply go to the website, download the prompt into your preferred personal Agent, and you are up and running.

You choose the moments that should prompt a donation, whether that's money saved on a refund, a personal milestone, or simply a good day. Your agent keeps an eye out for them, and when one happens, it suggests a modest gift. That gift could go to a cause you care about (every US nonprofit in good standing is hooked up to the system) or to a neighbor facing an urgent need. The agent suggests, and you decide. Nothing is given without your approval.

As we prepare for Thanksgiving, let’s put our agents to work with a new generous habit.

Send it around the table or to friends and see if we can’t maybe just tilt this AI moment a little bit more in the direction of our humanity this holiday.

Happy Thanksgiving, and cheers to the season of giving.

Special appreciation to: Sommer Chatwin, Mike Barborak, Will Fleming, @AHHFleischmann, Laura Wyatt, Kelli Kreps, Ken Joseph, Jonah Gorski, Sidley, @TheLaurelWay, and @nbshare

Personal AI agents are everywhere now, and the hard part is figuring out which ones you can actually use today. Here are 10 (5 from China, 5 from the West): who makes them, where to get them, what they're good at, and whether you can sign up.

Status is as of Nov 24, based on official sites and public reporting. I haven't hands-on tested all of them, so treat this as a map, not a review. Things change fast.

Quick take
Open now: Lingguang, WorkBuddy, Gemini Tasks (6 countries), Meta Muse (6 countries), OpenClaw (self-hosted).
Invite or waitlist: Xiaodou, Qwen Go!, OpenAI Dots, Claude Duet.
Still in gray-scale testing: WeChat Xiaowei.

CHINA

1. Xiaodou (小豆) | ByteDance, the team behind the Doubao chatbot
Where: https://t.co/ZhftCk7Jel (standalone app)
What it does: built around being proactive and remembering you. Once you connect apps like Douyin (China's TikTok), Feishu (ByteDance's workplace suite), your calendar or health data, it can flag price drops, expiring coupons and schedule clashes, and keep following up on tasks in the background.
Status: invite-only public beta with free credits

2. WeChat Xiaowei (小微) | Tencent
Where: top-left of the WeChat home screen (no separate site)
What it does: lives inside WeChat. You can "ask Xiaowei" from 30+ places (chats, Moments, official accounts, Channels), and it can operate WeChat features and mini-programs for you. Tencent says it already had 30 million daily users during testing (Q3 earnings).
Status: gray-scale testing, no date for full rollout

3. Qwen Go! | Alibaba
Where: inside the Qwen app (https://t.co/TsAnb7I5DH)
What it does: multi-step errands across Alibaba's ecosystem: ordering, price comparison, car maintenance, booking workouts, plus cloud phone and cloud PC.
Status: join the waitlist in the app, rolling out in batches

4. Lingguang 2.0 (灵光) | Ant Group, the company behind Alipay
Where: https://t.co/aIUdcJjd1M
What it does: cross-session memory plus its own cloud machine, so tasks keep running after you close the chat, like watching a flight price after booking or finding forgotten auto-renewals in your Alipay bills. Permissions go through one authorization system and can be revoked anytime.
Status: available in app stores now

5. WorkBuddy | Tencent
Where: https://t.co/LOLhPHksVM
What it does: Tencent pitches it as a personal agent for office work, with desktop apps for Windows and macOS.
Status: open download, free tier with 500 credits a month

WEST

6. Muse | Meta
Where: https://t.co/kBOtv4HYu4
What it does: each user gets a secure cloud VM; it connects to email, calendar and Instagram, and you can chat with it in WhatsApp. It asks before sending emails or paying. WIRED's roundup called it the easiest to get started with.
Status: free, but only in the US, Canada, Japan, Singapore, Mexico and Australia

7. Dots | OpenAI
Where: https://t.co/E6wYh0CSRo
What it does: runs on GPT-6 Astra with its own cloud computer, connects to 4,000+ apps and works in the background. Ranked first overall in WIRED's roundup.
Status: ChatGPT Pro and Business plans; only a small group of Plus users so far

8. Claude Duet | Anthropic
Where: https://t.co/FjXJVITpcI
What it does: geared toward work and small teams: daily briefings, keeping an eye on connected apps, confirming before it acts. Anthropic admits personal errands like booking tickets aren't its strength yet.
Status: US only, Pro / Max / Ultra, waitlist

9. Gemini Tasks (formerly Spark) | Google
Where: https://t.co/NhlCB1UGSZ
What it does: switch from Chat to Tasks inside the Gemini app and hand off work, no extra app needed.
Status: free since Nov 17 in the US, Canada, Australia, India, Japan and South Korea, 18+

10. OpenClaw | open-source community
Where: https://t.co/4XPTNrfEFB
What it does: runs on your own device, plugs into 20+ chat channels, and your data stays with you. Around 395k GitHub stars; many Chinese "XX Claw" products are built on it.
Status: free and open source, self-hosted

Which one are you using, and for what?
